hints.title: Self-Joining Course Enrollments
hints.text: Join the enrollments table to itself on student identifier with the condition that course1 is strictly less than course2.

hints.title: Aggregate by Pair
hints.text: Group by course1_id and course2_id and count distinct student occurrences.

hints.title: Rank by Maximum Frequency
hints.text: Use a window ranking function or subquery to select all pairs tied for the maximum count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH PairCounts AS (
    SELECT 
        e1.course_id AS course1_id,
        e2.course_id AS course2_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT e1.student_id) AS pair_count
    FROM Enrollments e1
    JOIN Enrollments e2 
      ON e1.student_id = e2.student_id 
     AND e1.course_id < e2.course_id
    GROUP BY e1.course_id, e2.course_id
),
Ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        course1_id,
        course2_id,
        pair_count,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pair_count DESC) AS rnk
    FROM PairCounts
)
SELECT 
    course1_id,
    course2_id,
    pair_count
FROM Ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY course1_id ASC, course2_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Here m is the number of enrollments and k is the average number of courses per student.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: A cross join without self-joining on matching student IDs produces an infeasible Cartesian product.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Materializing the pair counts in a CTE simplifies dense ranking for ties.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Expects understanding of self-joins with ordering filter e1.course_id < e2.course_id and handling ties using DENSE_RANK.
